extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media professionals, and researchers interested in solutions-focused reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and standards for producing 'solutions journalism' — reporting that focuses on responses to social problems and evaluates whether and how those responses work. Covers evidence standards, story balance, pitfalls (feel-good/advocacy), and recommended emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous, evidence-based reporting on responses
rubrics_metrics.description: "Solutions journalism is rigorous, evidence-based reporting on the responses to social problems."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be anchored in credible evidence; proponents argue an evidence-based approach diminishes the risk of bias. Avoid treating responses as mere anecdotes or untested theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify root causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "identify the root causes of a social problem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should go beyond symptoms to explain underlying drivers of the problem so the response is grounded in an accurate diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominently highlight a response or responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "prominently highlight a response, or responses, to that problem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response(s) should be a clear focus of the story (not merely an afterthought) and presented with sufficient detail about implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present evidence of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "present evidence of the impact of that response."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable or documented outcomes, evaluation findings, or credible indicators showing whether the response had an effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how and why the response is working or not
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "explain how and why the response is working, or not working."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide causal or mechanism-level analysis so readers understand the conditions under which the response succeeds or fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer insight into complex systems when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: "When possible, solutions stories also present an insight that helps people better understand how complex systems work, and how they can be improved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond describing a specific program, stories should illuminate system dynamics or generalizable lessons that inform broader decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate from 'good news' — avoid superficiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents distinguish solutions journalism from so-called "good news" reporting, which is characterized by a superficial presentation of a response without careful analysis of whether the response is effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: uplifting or feel-good pieces that spotlight positive outcomes without scrutiny. Maintain analytical rigor rather than merely positive tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess proven (working) responses rather than untested theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "assess responses that are working today, as opposed to untested theories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage of implemented responses with observable results rather than speculative or experimental ideas without demonstrated impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize innovation over personalities or institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions stories "tend to place more emphasis on the innovation than on a person or institution responsible for that innovation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the method or program itself (its design and outcomes) rather than hero profiles that personalize or obscure the mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid advocacy and calls to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics warn about potential bias and advocacy; proponents respond that "solutions stories should not be connected to a 'call to action' for readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain journalistic distance. Evidence-based reporting should inform rather than advocate for particular policies or solicit direct action from readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story balance between problem and solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions' rule of thumb: "no more than one-third of the paper should describe the problem, while at least two-thirds should be devoted to solutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the coverage allocates sufficient space to the response, its implementation, evidence, and analysis rather than concentrating on the problem description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require subject expertise to avoid oversimplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics note that many complex social issues "do not have clear causes or clear solutions," which "may require reporters pursuing solutions stories to have considerable expertise in a subject area."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should seek expertise, rigorous analysis, and nuanced context so solutions reporting does not yield simplistic or misleading conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hero worship and 'feel-good' storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A common criticism is that solutions journalism "easily devolves into 'feel-good' storytelling or hero worship, rather than critically examining important issues in society."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively guard against narrative choices that unduly personalize or sentimentalize a response; instead interrogate effectiveness, trade-offs, limits, and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evidence to minimize bias while acknowledging limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents assert that an "evidence-based approach to reporting diminishes the risk of bias."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While evidence reduces bias, reporters should still disclose limitations, uncertainties, and contexts where evidence may be weak or non-generalizable.
